title: SIEM export readiness, mapping strategy, and connector guidance
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures practical guidance for shipping SIEM export connectors (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel) from Redwood Inference, plus a customer-readiness checklist and a recommended field-mapping strategy for audit/evidence events. It is intended to be an operational reference for engineering, security, and customer-facing SREs when onboarding customers or validating connector changes.

Background & scope:
- Background: multiple customers ask to forward audit logs, inference traces, and evidence artifacts into their SIEM. We support several delivery mechanisms (HTTP/HEC, syslog, cloud-native ingestion). Past integrations revealed subtle differences in expected field names, rate limits, and PII-redaction expectations.
- Scope: mapping strategy and connector-level requirements for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics). Includes: schema baseline, transport/reliability constraints, redaction rules, customer checklist, and test/validation plan.
- Non-goals: this is not a full deployment runbook for Private installs (see private-deployments/export-runbook) and not a final legal PII policy.

Key objectives:
1) Define a minimal, stable audit schema that covers RBAC v2 events, inference invocation metadata, and evidence pointers.
2) Provide concrete guidance per SIEM (HEC/Datadog/Log Analytics) to avoid mapping mistakes and ingestion failures.
3) List customer network/security readiness items and performance expectations.
4) Provide a short validation plan and smoke tests for on-boarding.

Minimal audit event schema (recommended canonical fields) - 1 JSON event per action:
- event_id: uuidv4 (string)
- occurred_at: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (e.g. 2026-02-25T14:23:03Z)
- tenant_id: string (customer org id)
- principal: string (user.email || service-account-id)
- principal_id: string (internal id if available)
- actor_type: {user|service|system} (string)
- action: string (e.g., model.generate, model.load, policy.evaluate, rbac.grant)
- resource: string (resource path or resource type e.g., models/anthropic-2)
- resource_id: string
- outcome: {success|failure|denied|skipped} (string)
- request_id: string (trace id correlated with request pipeline)
- session_id: string (optional)
- duration_ms: integer as string (latency)
- event_category: {audit|telemetry|evidence} (string)
- model_name: string (if applicable)
- model_variant: string (optional)
- tokens_in: string (numeric)
- tokens_out: string (numeric)
- cost_estimate_usd: string (optional)
- evidence_url: string (signed url or pointer; MUST be redacted if PII present)
- raw_request_summary: string (short text summary; avoid full prompt content unless customer approved)
- ip: string (IP address of caller; treat as PII)
- metadata: string (free-form JSON string for additional fields)

Notes on schema choices:
- Keep the primary fields flat at top-level for compatibility with Splunk/Datadog indexing. Avoid deeply nested objects; store large payloads or complex shapes as escaped JSON in metadata or evidence object.
- All numeric values should be strings to avoid automatic data type coercion differences across SIEMs.

PII and redaction guidance (customer-facing defaults):
- Default policy: redact full prompts/inputs and any attachment contents unless customer explicitly requests and signs a data-handling amendment. Replace with "[REDACTED_INPUT]" and store truncated summary in raw_request_summary.
- IP addresses, user emails should be hashed (sha256) when exported unless the customer requests otherwise. Provide original values in private-deployments-only with proper KMS controls.
- Evidence artifacts containing PII must not be exported to customer SIEMs unless part of an approved evidence-export package; instead export metadata pointers and a unique evidence_id.

Per-SIEM guidance
1) Splunk (HTTP Event Collector - HEC)
- Transport: POST to https://{splunk-host}:8088/services/collector/event with HEC token header X-Splunk-Token.
- Expected body shape: either single JSON event or HEC-batched array. Recommended envelope: {"time": <epoch>, "host":"redwood-inference", "source":"redwood:inference:audit", "sourcetype":"_json", "index":"<customer-index>", "event": <canonical-event-json>}
- sourcetype recommendation: "redwood:inference:audit" (helps signal extraction).
- Batch sizing: keep <= 5MB per request and <= 500 events. Use gzip compression.
- Rate/throughput: treat HEC limits as soft default; implement client-side throttling and exponential backoff (start 500ms, max 60s).
- Idempotency: include event_id and request_id to enable dedup logic on Splunk side if needed.
- Truncation: Splunk will drop fields that exceed indexed size; ensure important fields (event_id, occurred_at, outcome) are first-class.

2) Datadog Logs
- Transport: HTTP to https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input with API key (DD-API-KEY).
- Envelope: Datadog expects top-level attributes like "ddsource":"redwood", "service":"inference", "hostname":"", and the JSON event as the body. Add ddtags for tenant_id and region.
- Rate limits: Datadog enforces a ingestion rate per account; implement batching ~200 events/req and compress. On 429, honor Retry-After header.
- Parsing: Datadog will flatten fields automatically. Recommend prefixing custom fields with "rdw_" (e.g., rdw_event_id) to prevent accidental collisions with customer fields.

3) Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Data Collector API)
- Transport: Azure Monitor Data Collector API requires workspaceId and shared key. Post to https://<workspaceId>.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01.
- Body: JSON array of objects (each our canonical event).
- Content-Type: application/json; create signature header per docs.
- Type (table name): set to Redwood_Inference_Audit (avoid spaces).
- Perf: Azure expects reasonably sized batches; stay under 30MB.
- Field mapping: Log Analytics will create dynamic fields; ensure occurred_at maps to TimeGenerated by passing a TimeGenerated key or using occurred_at as iso string.

Connector reliability & operational requirements
- Delivery semantics: best-effort with retries; connectors should aim for exactly-once where supported (idempotency via event_id), but fall back to at-least-once with dedup guidance.
- Backpressure: if SIEM returns 429 or network errors, connectors should: increase backoff, pause new reads after configurable failure threshold, surface alerts to SRE and to the customer via status webhook.
- Authentication: support token-based auth (HEC token, Datadog API key) and mTLS where customers require. Support rotating credentials without downtime (graceful token refresh).
- Observability: export internal metrics: events_sent, events_failed, events_retries, avg_latency_ms, last_success_timestamp, dropped_events_count, last_error. These metrics should be exposed to Redwood monitoring and optionally available to customers.

Customer readiness checklist (must be validated before enabling exports):
- Network egress: allow outbound to the SIEM endpoints (hostnames + IP ranges). Verify proxy allowances.
- Auth material: customer has HEC token / Datadog API key / Azure workspace id and shared key provisioned and validated.
- Indexing table: customer has an agreed index/name (Splunk index, Datadog service, Log Analytics table).
- Retention and legal: customer legal has signed off on retention and PII export policy.
- RBAC: limit who can enable/disable exports in console (console roles required) — map to RBAC v2 roles: security_admin or platform_ops.
- Load expectations: expected events-per-second and burst pattern documented; validate against connector throughput limits.

Testing & validation plan
1) Schema validation: send 10 synthetic events covering success/failure/evidence cases; confirm fields appear in target SIEM and timestamps parse as expected.
2) Perf test: ramp to expected sustained events/sec + 2x burst for 10 minutes; monitor for 429s or data loss.
3) Failure modes: simulate auth failure (invalid token), network blackhole, and SIEM 5xx responses; verify connector enters backoff and alerts.
4) End-to-end correlation: ensure request_id links SIEM events to internal traces (instrumentation via trace headers).
5) Redaction verification: confirm prompts and attachments are redacted or replaced per policy.

Sample event (canonical JSON, truncated for readability):
{
  "event_id": "b4d2f0a6-1d2c-4f9b-9a6a-2d7f4b6e7c9f",
  "occurred_at": "2026-02-25T14:23:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "org-7a9c",
  "principal": "alice@example.com",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "model.generate",
  "resource": "models/gptx-13b",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-992d3",
  "duration_ms": "134",
  "event_category": "evidence",
  "model_name": "gptx-13b",
  "tokens_in": "12",
  "tokens_out": "48",
  "evidence_url": "[REDACTED_EVIDENCE_URL]",
  "raw_request_summary": "Generate short product description (input redacted)"
}

Known limitations & open questions:
- Large evidence artifacts: current export must not stream large binary artifacts; plan is to provide pointer + out-of-band transfer (S3 presigned or secure artifact push).
- Field collisions: customers sometimes index custom fields that clash with ours (e.g., "service"). Recommend prefixing internal fields with rdw_.
- Advanced parsing: some customers prefer raw text in _raw for Splunk; we default to JSON structured events. Need product decision on offering both.
- E2E encryption to customer SIEM (mTLS) is supported but rollout requires extra onboarding steps; track rollout in JIRA-SEC-984.

Next steps:
- Get sign-off from product and legal on PII redaction defaults (owner: Priya Nair).
- Engineering: implement rdw_ prefix option and HEC batch size tuning (owner: Jordan Lee, PR: linked_artifacts).
- Customer success: update onboarding checklist and add a short network test script to the onboarding kit.

If you're reviewing this doc: please add comments inline or raise issues in JIRA-SEC-984. For immediate questions ping #security-siem on Slack.
